question: If sqrt{2}Cosec A=2secA find the value of tanA secA.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the given equation to **tan A**: √2 ÷ sin A = 2 ÷ cos A

⇒ cos A ÷ sin A = 2 ÷ √2

⇒ cot A = √2 ⇒ **tan A = 1/√2**

Using **sec²A = 1 + tan²A** ⇒ sec A = √(1 + 1/2) = √(3/2)

⇒ tan A × sec A = (1/√2) × (√3/√2) = √3/2

**∴ The correct answer is √3/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7b7ffef15d07a42f78d83d634b04eb82d51d5205df441e67c1113bf16a1ec008.png] 

**Given:** √2 cosec A = 2 sec A

**Formula:** cosec A = 1/sin A, sec A = 1/cos A, tan A = sin A/cos A

⇒ √2 / sin A = 2 / cos A

⇒ sin A / cos A = √2 / 2

⇒ tan A = 1 / √2

⇒ Let **Perpendicular (P)** = 1 and **Base (B)** = √2

⇒ **Hypotenuse (H)** = √(P² + B²) = √(1² + (√2)²) = √3

⇒ sec A = H / B = √3 / √2

⇒ tan A × sec A = (1 / √2) × (√3 / √2)

⇒ tan A × sec A = √3 / 2

**∴ The correct answer is √3/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental relations: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Ratio Definitions

tan θ = P/B, sec θ = H/B, and cosec θ = H/P where P, B, H are parts of a right-angled triangle.</p
